title: Ordeo component layout
description: Describes the composition and layout of one component and its parts. Tokens hold the styling; this file holds what the tokens cannot: which parts exist, how they nest, and how they are laid out. It is platform neutral and is consumed by tooling that generates the platform-specific code.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, so the IDE can validate the file.

components.description: Every renderable unit of this component. The first entry is the root; the rest are the parts it (or another part) references through slots. Each entry becomes one component in the generated code.

component.description: One renderable unit: the root component or one of its parts.

name.description: Unique name of this unit in PascalCase. Parts are prefixed with the name of the unit that contains them, e.g. `ButtonIcon` inside `Button`.

content.description: What this unit renders. `parts`: a container for other units, filled through `slots`. `text`: a run of text. `illustration`: a non-text visual such as an icon or spinner.

tokens.description: Token paths (dot separated, as in the token files) whose styles apply to this unit, e.g. `component.button.base`.

layout.description: How this unit arranges the parts in its slots. Omit it for units that have nothing to arrange.

type.description: Layout model. `flex` places the parts in a single line along `direction`.

justify.description: Distribution of the parts along the main axis.

align.description: Alignment of the parts on the cross axis.

features.description: Behavioural traits the generated code has to account for.

interactive.description: The unit reacts to user input and needs interaction states (hover, focus, pressed, disabled).

slots.description: Named places where the consumer supplies a part. Keys are the slot names in camelCase. Only allowed when `content` is `parts`.

required.description: Whether the consumer must fill this slot.

for.description: Name of the unit that fills this slot, or a list of units when more than one may fill it. Must match the `name` of a unit in this file.
